answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to a verifiable history of useful work, not to account count. A new identity starts behind a ridge: it may take small jobs, but larger payments and votes stay locked until independent, established peers vouch for work it completed. Each voucher risks slashing if the vouched agent cheats, so a fraudster cannot echo one cheap credential across thousands of clones. Forging a credible history then costs real work per identity, while an honest agent crosses the mesa one verified job at a time, and mass forgery stays unprofitable.
